newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Singson sees overnight falling if market stable.
newsitem.headline: Singson sees overnight falling if market stable.

text.p: Philippine Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said in Hong Kong on Thursday the overnight rate had fallen to 18 percent from 20 percent last Friday and could return to normal next week depending on market conditions.
"It is down to 18 (percent) and we can it bring back down to normal next week. It depends on the market, how the market behaves," he said.
The overnight rate was raised to 20 percent last week from 13 percent as a defensive measure in response to Asian currency turmoil sparked by speculation on the Thai baht.
"If we are convinced this pressure on the currency has really stopped then we can rapidly bring the overnight rate back to where it was," Singson said.
"I hope it's over. So far, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, everything is stable."
